facts.content: Patient reports 'struggling to breathe' after an insect sting.
facts.source_text: CC: “struggling to breathe” after insect sting

facts.content: Patient experienced a bee or wasp sting to the right arm a few minutes ago, resulting in a local erythematous rash, puncture mark, and mild soreness.
facts.source_text: HPI: Bee/wasp sting to R arm a few min ago → local erythematous rash, puncture mark, mild soreness

facts.content: Patient feels lips and tongue are 'weird' with mild shortness of breath now settled.
facts.source_text: feels lips/tongue “weird,” mild SOB now settled

facts.content: Patient is anxious about possible worsening of symptoms.
Patient has a history of eczema and episodic anxiety which was never medicated.
Patient is not currently taking any medications and has not taken any antihistamines yet.
facts.source_text: Meds: None; no antihistamine taken yet

facts.content: There is no known family history of anaphylaxis.
Patient is a computer scientist who lives alone and has a cat at home.
facts.source_text: SH: Computer scientist; lives alone; cat at home

facts.content: No swelling observed on lips, tongue, or oropharyngeal area.
Right arm has a small puncture with mild erythema and blotchiness, no obvious swelling or heat.
facts.source_text: R arm: small puncture with mild erythema/blotchiness, no obvious swelling/heat

facts.content: Localised allergic reaction to insect sting with no current signs of systemic reaction or anaphylaxis.
facts.source_text: Localised allergic reaction to insect sting; no current systemic/anaphylaxis signs

facts.content: Start over-the-counter antihistamine (chlorphenamine 4 mg PO q4–6h PRN or once-daily alternative).
facts.source_text: Start OTC antihistamine (chlorphenamine 4 mg PO q4–6h PRN or once-daily alternative)

facts.content: Red-flag education provided: lip/tongue swelling, stridor, worsening SOB requires immediate 999/ED contact.
facts.source_text: Red-flag education: lip/tongue swelling, stridor, worsening SOB → 999/ED immediately

facts.content: Monitor sting site and seek urgent review if spreading erythema, heat, or pain occurs which may require antibiotics.
facts.source_text: Monitor sting site; if spreading erythema, heat, pain → urgent review ± antibiotics

facts.content: Provide information link on anaphylaxis and offer reassurance; encourage low threshold for re-contact if symptoms change or recurrent reactions occur.
facts.source_text: Provide anaphylaxis info link; reassurance; encourage low threshold for re-contact if symptoms change or recurrent reactions occur
